Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement is ready to circulate the order form but we need two clarifications before we route to our AP team: 

1) Which legal entity should be on the invoice? Our PO system needs the remit-to to match a tax id.
2) Can you confirm the net terms (Net 30 vs Net 45) and whether Redwood will accept a single invoice for the full commitment or if you’ll split by tranche?
3) On taxes — we are an EU subsidiary paying from the US. Do you require a VAT/resale certificate, or will ClearSky be responsible for VAT/reverse-charge?

Attaching the draft order form you sent to our commercial team.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — targeting PO by end of week.

Best,
Maya Patel
Director, Procurement
ClearSky Health

Date: 2027-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice recipient and VAT

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps from our side: 

1) Invoice recipient: Our standard hosted-sales entity is "Redwood Inference, Inc." (US EIN on file). We can invoice that entity for the committed amount. If you need invoices routed to ClearSky’s EU entity, we can discuss multi-entity invoicing but that will need finance/legal signoff.

2) Net terms: Our typical is Net 30. Sales is open to Net 45 for larger deals with an approved credit note — karthik, can you confirm ops feasibility? We generally prefer single invoices per tranche (we can do monthly consolidated invoices within a tranche).

3) Taxes: For EU customers paying from a US org, we typically invoice gross and the customer handles VAT/resale certificates. If you can supply a VAT certificate or resale exemption, we can record that and annotate invoices — but Redwood will not withhold VAT.

I'm looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Laura (Finance) to confirm we can (a) keep Redwood Inference, Inc. as remit-to, (b) accept Net 45 exception if Ops approves, and (c) note the VAT cert on file so AP won't auto-withhold.

Goal: get a PO by Friday, then legal redline within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi team — quick legal perspective and suggested redline language for the Order Form / MSA mapping: 

- Invoice Recipient: We will invoice "Redwood Inference, Inc." unless ClearSky executes the Order Form on behalf of a different ClearSky subsidiary and provides a signed PO referencing that entity. If you require Redwood to invoice an EU entity, we need the EU entity's legal name, tax id, and a signed Addendum (we can add a short clause enabling split invoicing).

Suggested redline (Order Form, Invoicing section):
"Invoices shall be issued by Redwood Inference, Inc. to the legal entity identified on the Purchase Order. Customer shall provide any tax-exemption or VAT registration documentation at least five (5) business days prior to the first invoice date. Customer remains responsible for any withholding or indirect tax liabilities unless otherwise agreed in writing."

- Net Terms: We are comfortable with Net 45 as an exception. Add: "Net 45 subject to credit approval and payment milestone schedule agreed in Appendix A."

- Taxes: We cannot accept liability for Customer VAT unless explicitly agreed. Request a VAT or resale certificate be uploaded to the shared drive and referenced in the Order Form.

I will prepare a brief addendum and send a redline back to you (Hannah) this afternoon.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal_redline_track_changes.docx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice recipient and VAT

Hannah / team — ops & finance notes: 

- We can operationalize Net 45 on a case-by-case basis. Need a 2-week lead time to configure credit hold exceptions and billing cadence in Zuora. If ClearSky needs Net 45, ask them to confirm in the PO and include the billing contact for disputes.

- Tranching / invoicing: we support (a) single invoice per tranche or (b) monthly consolidated invoices. For clarity I recommend: "Invoices will be issued monthly and will reference the applicable tranche; the first invoice will be issued upon activation of services."

- Practical ask for AP: Please have ClearSky attach their VAT/resale certificate (if applicable) and the remit-to PO number when they send the PO. Without that, finance will route through our global tax team and it may delay payment.

I'll update the internal billing playbook and share the checklist for onboarding ClearSky once Kimberly's redline is final.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Operations Manager
